title: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
abstract: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.

bite.hook: Pretty good measurements and Petz maps are unified in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power.
tldr: Studied optimal quantum measurements and recovery maps using explicit approximations.
Unified pretty good measurements and Petz maps within a semidefinite programming framework.
Proved a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power.
bite.whyItMatters: Finding optimal quantum operations is notoriously difficult. Better approximations and unified frameworks make it easier to design robust quantum communication and error-correction protocols.
bite.eli5: In quantum physics, figuring out the absolute best way to measure or fix a broken quantum state is extremely hard. Scientists use clever shortcuts called 'pretty good measurements,' and this paper figures out a way to supercharge and unify these shortcuts.
